s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, cutaneous vascular lesions with localized erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
salient_findings: Multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
Firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques with irregular borders
Thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels dispersed between thickened collagen bundles
key_facts: Female patient in her late 20s
2-year history of skin lesions
Lesions located on left upper arm, left axilla, and lateral thoracic region
No triggers such as local infection, insect bite, or trauma occurred before lesion appearance
No fever, weight loss, or fatigue
Histopathological examination showed irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels
Endothelial cells were plump but displayed no significant cytologic atypia
Immunohistochemistry results positive for CD31, CD34, Ki-67 (<1%)
Immunohistochemistry results negative for podoplanin (D2-40), human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, cutaneous vascular lesions with localized erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
salient_findings: Multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
Firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques with irregular borders
Thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels dispersed between thickened collagen bundles
key_facts: Female patient in her late 20s
2-year history of skin lesions
Lesions located on left upper arm, left axilla, and lateral thoracic region
No triggers such as local infection, insect bite, or trauma occurred before lesion appearance
No fever, weight loss, or fatigue
Histopathological examination showed irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels
Endothelial cells were plump but displayed no significant cytologic atypia
Immunohistochemistry results positive for CD31, CD34, Ki-67 (<1%)
Immunohistochemistry results negative for podoplanin (D2-40), human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, along with the histopathological findings of irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels and plump endothelial cells, is consistent with lichenoid mycosis fungoides. The immunohistochemistry results, including positivity for CD31 and CD34, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: While mycosis fungoides is a consideration, the lichenoid variant is more specific to the patient's presentation and histopathological findings.

rejected.label: primary cutaneous marginal zone lymphoma
rejected.why: The lack of significant cytologic atypia and negativity for podoplanin (D2-40) make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: dermatitis
rejected.why: The patient's lesions are more infiltrated and have a longer duration than typical dermatitis, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: discoid lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and histopathological findings do not match the typical characteristics of discoid lupus erythematosus, such as follicular plugging and periadnexal inflammation.
